fullPassage: Have you ever noticed that the buttons on men's clothing and women's clothing are arranged differently? On men's shirts, the buttons are located on the wearer's right-hand side. On women's shirts, they are on the left-hand side. This is because of a tradition that began when clothing with buttons was expensive. Women who were wealthy enough to buy button-up clothing rarely dressed themselves. Instead, they were dressed by maids, who, like most people, were usually right-handed. Therefore, clothing makers made it easier for the maids to fasten the buttons by putting them on the wearer's left-hand side. Today, most people dress themselves and the placement of buttons can differ depending on the designer or brand, but many clothing makers are still reluctant to change such a well-known tradition.

det.korean: ② beginning → began: a tradition that began에서 관계대명사절의 동사로 과거시제 began이 와야 한다.
det.analysis:

✅ ② beginning: a tradition that began when에서 that은 주격 관계대명사이고, 주절 시제(This is)와 맞춰 과거형 began이 와야 한다. 현재분사 beginning은 어법상 틀림 ←정답

❌ ③ dressed: they were dressed by maids에서 수동태(be + p.p.) 구문. 올바름

❌ ④ depending: can differ depending on에서 분사구문(~에 따라). 올바름
det.tip: 관계대명사절에서 동사의 시제: 주절이 현재(is)이더라도 과거 사실을 서술하면 과거형(began) 사용. beginning(현재분사)은 동사 자리에 올 수 없다.

det.tip: by + 동명사(V-ing): '~함으로써'의 수단/방법. by put(동사원형) ❌ → by putting ✅.

det.korean: ④ must → can: 단추 배치가 디자이너에 따라 '달라질 수 있다(can differ)'는 가능성의 문맥에서 must(반드시)는 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① arranged: are arranged differently에서 수동태(be + p.p.). '배열되다'의 의미로 올바름

det.tip: can(가능성: ~할 수 있다) vs must(의무/확신: ~해야 한다/~임에 틀림없다). 맥락에 따른 조동사 선택이 핵심.

questions.passage: Have you ever noticed that the buttons on men's clothing and women's clothing are arranged differently? On men's shirts, the buttons are located on the wearer's right-hand side. On women's shirts, they are on the left-hand side. This is because of a tradition that began when clothing with buttons was expensive. Women who were wealthy enough to buy button-up clothing rarely dressed themselves. Instead, they were dressed by maids, who, like most people, were usually right-handed. Therefore, clothing makers made it easier for the maids to fasten the buttons by putting them on the wearer's left-hand side.
